annotations.title: A country's economy from its own statistics office and central bank

description: A country's economy from the statistics office or central bank that publishes it: inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, policy rate, 10-year yield, exchange rate, industrial production, retail sales, wages, house prices, the OECD's leading indicator, for 70 countries and the euro area, one or up to 30 side by side (G7, G20, EU), or all of one country's. Any series by its publisher's code (IMF, BIS, ECB, Eurostat, OECD, ONS, Bank of Japan, 17 more). check: true compares a second official publisher.

check.description: Also read the same figure from a second official publisher (the IMF, BIS, OECD or Eurostat) and compare the latest period both report.

countries.description: Several side by side, or a group: G7, G20, EU, euro area members, BRICS, Nordics, ASEAN, Latin America. Up to 30.

country.description: One country or the euro area: a name (Brazil, South Korea, euro area) or an ISO code (BR, KOR).

measure.description: inflation, core_inflation, unemployment, gdp_growth, policy_rate, ten_year_yield, exchange_rate, industrial_production, retail_sales, wages, leading_indicator (the OECD's), consumer_confidence, business_confidence, government_debt, money_supply, central_bank_assets or house_prices, or all (one country's every measure, the default for one country); plain words work ("jobless rate", "10-year bond yield").

periods.description: Observations to return, latest last. Default 13 (one country), 1 (several).

series.description: Any series by its publisher's own code instead: imf:, bis:, ecb:, eurostat:, oecd:, ilo:, fred:, statcan:, boc:, ons:, boe:, boj:, mof:, rba:, abs:, bcb:, ibge:, riksbank:, scb:, ssb:, norges:, snb:, bbk:, boi: (e.g. "statcan:2062815", "eurostat:une_rt_m?geo=DE&s_adj=SA&age=TOTAL&sex=T&unit=PC_ACT").

start.description: Return everything from this date (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD) instead, up to 600 observations.

name: world_series

outputSchema.description: one country: rows are periods (oldest first) with the value, latest and year_ago beside them; several: a row per country with its latest period, value, quote, publisher and series.

title: A country's economy from its own statistics office and central bank
